# The shared visual grammar {#visual-grammar}

This chapter explains the reusable building blocks that every later chapter
assumes: themes, sizing, palettes, saving, and composite assembly.

## Theme

`glyphome_theme()` is a minimal ggplot2 theme tuned for composite figures:

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
source("R/glyphome-common.R")

ggplot(mtcars, aes(wt, mpg)) +
  geom_point() +
  glyphome_theme(base_size = 10) +
  labs(title = "Title in bold", subtitle = "Subtitle in muted grey")
```

Key choices:

- Bold title, muted subtitle, captions on the left.
- Minor grid removed; major grid in `#e9ecef` at hairline weight.
- Strip text bold to anchor faceted panels.
- Legend titles bold, key size compact.

A void variant `glyphome_theme_void()` is used for spatial maps and
embeddings where axes are meaningless.

## Role-based panel sizing

Every panel in the suite is assigned a *role*. The role drives the
dimensions of the saved PNG:

| Role        | Width × Height (in) | Used for                                         |
|-------------|---------------------|--------------------------------------------------|
| hero        | 16 × 12             | Headline composite (e.g. `survivora` landscape)  |
| primary     | 13 × 10             | Module main figures                              |
| supporting  | 10 × 8              | Side panels, single-axis summaries               |
| auxiliary   | 8 × 6               | Diagnostic plots                                 |

```{r eval=FALSE}
glyphome_save(p, "figures/my_figure.png", role = "hero")
```

This is the implementation of the figure-composition rule that
*"consistency does not mean equal panel size."* Information density and
interpretive importance dictate area; the role label makes that decision
explicit and reproducible.

## Palettes

Each module owns a domain-tuned categorical palette named `<module>_*_pal()`
or `<module>_*_palette()`. The cell-type palette in `densweave_ct_pal()` is
the canonical 30-colour atlas palette and is intentionally consistent with
`uncertainr_celltype_palette()` so that figures from different modules read
together when assembled into a manuscript.

```{r eval=FALSE}
source("packages/densweave/R/densweave.R")
densweave_ct_pal()
```

Continuous scales follow domain convention: `viridis::mako` for density,
`viridis::magma` for expression intensity, `gradient2(blue/white/red)` for
signed deltas, and `OrRd`/`YlOrRd` for hazard or risk.

## Saving conventions

PNG is the default for the rendered figure set because it is what
manuscript review processes expect. `glyphome_save()` writes at 300 dpi with
white background; vector formats are available via `ggplot2::ggsave()` for
final composition in Illustrator or Inkscape.

## Composite figures

All composite figures use **patchwork**. The pattern is:

```{r eval=FALSE}
library(patchwork)

(p1 | p2 | p3) /
  (p4 + plot_layout(widths = c(2, 1))) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Module: figure title",
    subtitle = "One-line message of the figure"
  ) &
  glyphome_theme()
```

The `&` operator applies the theme to every panel in the patchwork; this is
how visual consistency is enforced across panels with different geom types.

::: design-notes
**Design notes.** A composite is not a grid. The role-based size table
should be applied even within one PNG file: hero panel ~25–40 % of total
area, auxiliary panels ≤ 12 %. See chapter \@ref(composing-figures).
:::
